$comment: PHASE 1 · build config for the NivXMachines Workspace frontend
(workspace.nivxmachines.com). OWNER LOCK · Q1 A · Q2 A · Q3 B · Q4 B · Q5 A.
INERT FOR THE EXISTING DEPLOYMENT. Only the config at a deployment's
configured Root Directory is read. The repo-root vercel.json (which
builds apps/nivxray-xdr) is untouched and still governs the existing
deployment, so this file CANNOT change what that deployment produces.
It takes effect only for a deployment whose Root Directory is
`frontend`.
WHY THE ENV VARS ARE IN buildCommand AND NOT IN A .env FILE — read
before changing anything here. craco.config.js line 3 calls
`require('dotenv').config()` at module load, which loads `.env` into
process.env BEFORE react-scripts' own env loader runs. dotenv never
overwrites an existing variable, so `.env` WINS over `.env.production`
in this project — the opposite of stock CRA precedence. A
`.env.production` file was tried and PROVEN not to take effect: the
build still inlined the preview backend URL 22 times. Real shell
variables (what buildCommand sets) are the only reliable override,
because dotenv will not overwrite them either. Verified: 23
occurrences of the production URL and 0 of the preview URL in the
emitted bundle.
REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL = https://nivxray.nivxforge.com is a deliberate
TEMPORARY_MIGRATION_DEPENDENCY (owner decision). It is the only proven
production API today. Phase 4 establishes the permanent API origin and
the Workspace is rebuilt against it. Because of this dependency,
nivxray.nivxforge.com MUST NOT be retired after Phase 1.
REACT_APP_NIVX_FLAG_* = disabled is required, not cosmetic. `.env`
sets all three to `shadow`, and craco's dotenv load means `.env` would
otherwise ship the /v2/* shadow surfaces switched ON in production.
Owner decision Q4 = B: routes retained, flags OFF.
CI=false because CRA promotes warnings to errors when CI is truthy and
this app carries 9 react-hooks/exhaustive-deps advisories. They are
lint advisories, not defects; fixing them changes effect timing, which
is not acceptable during a migration.
rewrites: WITHOUT this, /auto-investigate returns 404 on a static host
while / works — the exact symptom that looks like 'the tool is
missing'.
scripts/verify-production-build.js is chained after the build and FAILS
it if the emitted bundle embeds a preview origin, embeds an unapproved
or missing API origin, or ships a /v2/* shadow flag switched on. It
inspects the ARTEFACT, not process.env, precisely because the dotenv
precedence trap above means the environment can look right while the
bundle is wrong.
$installComment: repository does not satisfy frontend/package.json: 17 top-level
dependencies are missing, four of them runtime (@xyflow/react, dagre,
konva, react-konva). A regenerated lockfile exists in the working
tree (649,903 B, blob f69fa5aa) but the repository still holds the
old one (588,753 B, blob be098679) — verified through the GitHub API,
not the CDN. The push captures source files but not this lockfile, so
--frozen-lockfile would fail the install on every deploy, which is
exactly how the first XDR build died.
Trade-off accepted knowingly: yarn resolves the ranges at build time,
so a newer patch/minor may be picked up. The safety net is the
ARTEFACT check, not the lockfile — scripts/verify-production-build.js
fails the build if the wrong API origin, a preview origin or an
enabled shadow flag ever reaches the bundle. Restore
--frozen-lockfile once the regenerated lockfile is actually committed.
